chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a man who bought a slave girl whose owner had not yet had intercourse with her: Does he clear her womb? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. I said: A slave girl who has not yet menstruated, what is done with her? He (peace be upon him) said: Her case is difficult, except that if he has intercourse with her, he should not ejaculate into her until it becomes clear to him if she is pregnant. I said: And in how much time does it become clear to him? He (peace be upon him) said: In forty-five nights.

key_terms.اسْتِبْرَاءُ الرَّحِمِ: Clearing the womb (waiting period to confirm pregnancy status)

ai.seo_question: What is the istibra' period for a non-menstruating slave girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the 'istibra'' period for a pre-pubescent slave girl, ruling that if the master has not yet had intercourse with her, he must wait forty-five nights after the first act to confirm the absence of pregnancy. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the 'clearing of the womb' is contingent upon actual sexual contact, distinguishing it from cases where the previous owner had already impregnated her.
